## [0.11.0] - 2026-07-29

An **engine correctness release**, with HTTP/2 as its headline. The protocol work is the new capability: the engine's code has set `CURL_HTTP_VERSION_2TLS` for a while, but the linked libcurl never had HTTP/2 in it - vcpkg's default `curl` port ships without nghttp2 - so every request ran HTTP/1.1 regardless of what was asked for. Around that sits a substantial pass over load-test accuracy: the rate the generator actually delivers, when a run ends, whether stopping one stops it, and whether the metrics it reports are the metrics it measured. The app side is a rebuild of the response viewer and the editors feeding it, plus a documentation site.

### Added

- **Real HTTP/2 negotiation**, on both Send and load test. The engine's `curl` dependency now requests the `http2` feature, pulling in nghttp2, so the option the engine was already setting finally does something. A build-time test asserts the capability bit so a rebuild cannot silently drop back to a 1.1-only libcurl.
- **One Protocol control**, in the request builder's **Settings** tab, governing Send and load test alike. `Auto` lets ALPN negotiate (curl's own default); `HTTP/1.1` forces it; `HTTP/2` attempts h2 over TLS and falls back to 1.1 over plain `http://`, which is curl's `2TLS` semantics and deliberately silent, since a URL is often an unresolved `{{variable}}` when you set the field.
- **A Default HTTP Version setting** seeds the protocol a newly created request starts with. It is a write-time default only: changing it never alters a request already saved, which matters for a load-testing tool where a global toggle silently changing every stored request's protocol would invalidate comparisons against historical runs.
- **The response's Raw tab shows the protocol that was actually negotiated**, instead of the hardcoded `HTTP/1.1` it printed before no matter what ran. Run history and a run's final report show the protocol that was *requested* - a load run makes many exchanges and has no single negotiated value, and the requested setting is what is meaningful when comparing two runs.
- **MCP's `run_request` and `start_load_run`** accept the same `httpVersion` choice, so an agent can ask for HTTP/2 the way the app does.
- **Atomic bulk import via `POST /import/apply`**, with an engine-owned id map. An import is now one transaction that either lands whole or not at all, instead of a sequence of per-resource writes that could half-apply.
- **Postman environment and globals exports** are importable, not just collections.
- **Pre-request scripts can mutate the outgoing request.** A `pm.request` change now reaches the wire rather than being computed and discarded.
- **A documentation site** at [athrvk.github.io/vayu](https://athrvk.github.io/vayu/), built from `docs/` with MkDocs Material and published on every merge.
- **Load-test ceilings are a setting** rather than compile-time constants.

### Changed

- **Run time series are stored as wide per-tick rows plus a run summary**, rather than a row per metric per tick. A completed run now carries its own summary instead of the report recomputing one from sampled rows on every open.
- **The response viewer was rebuilt** - tabs, toolbar, Raw, Console and Tests - and the HTTP-exchange UI consolidated behind one timing descriptor and one sampled-exchange shell, so the live pane and a stored run's pane are the same components rather than two implementations that drifted.
- **The Body panel and the key/value editor behind Params and Headers were rebuilt**, with `{{variable}}` completion in the editors.
- **Create and update are separate verbs** across collections, requests and environments, under one null-vs-absent rule: on create, absent and `null` both mean "use the default"; on update, absent means "keep" and `null` means "reset". A field with no default rejects `null` with a 400 rather than ignoring the write.
- **Settings entries can be a labelled picker**, not just a number or a toggle. A new `enum` config type with an `options` column of `{value, label}` pairs backs the Default HTTP Version setting and is available to any future picker-style setting.
- **A run's redirect policy is reported by the API.** `followRedirects` / `maxRedirects` have been stored on every run since 0.10.0 but never left the database; they now ride with `httpVersion` into both `GET /runs`'s compact summary and a run's final report. No screen displays them yet - this makes them available to anything reading the API.
- **One auth editor and one mode registry** serve both the request and collection hosts.
- **Toasts** are built on the shadcn/Radix primitive, theme-aware, and no longer sit on top of the Dock.
- **CI splits into app, engine and installer jobs**, so a failure names which half broke, and the engine matrix is skipped for docs-only changes.

### Fixed

- **A constant-rate run now delivers the rate it was asked for and ends at its deadline**, and duration units are read as written rather than assumed.
- **Metrics are correct under load.** Bounded stores, atomic histograms, and a real failed-request count instead of one that omitted transport errors. A separate fix caps the collector's pre-allocation so a long high-rate run cannot wedge.
- **Stopping or deleting a run actually stops it.** Deleting a running run used to remove its rows while a detached worker kept writing new ones against the same id, orphaning them and letting a run partially un-delete itself as it finished. Run workers are also joined on shutdown rather than detached.
- **`POST /runs` validates its config before the run row exists**, so a rejected request leaves nothing behind.
- **Response buffering is bounded**, the wire method is preserved, and timing on a failed transfer is clamped rather than reported as a wild value.
- **Resource writes reject wrong-shape object fields.** `{"variables": 42}` used to store `42` and return 200; every reader then degraded quietly and the request went out bare.
- **A design run keeps a variable's `createdAt`** instead of resetting it.
- **The GraphQL `Content-Type` header is taken back** when the body mode changes away from GraphQL.
- **The whole drawer row is clickable**, not just its label; tooltips share one delay set at the app root; and the response tabs' rules are visible in both themes.

### Internal

`docs/architecture.md` claimed the engine's libcurl gave "HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3" - wrong before this release, since HTTP/2 was not linked, and still wrong after it, since HTTP/3 is an explicit non-goal requiring ngtcp2 + nghttp3 and pinning the TLS backend to OpenSSL. Corrected, along with a pass over the engine API reference, DB schema and MCP docs. A dead-config and unguarded-throw sweep closed the engine's hygiene tail. The label system gained an `area:mcp` label and an automatic release label on `VERSION` changes, `CODEOWNERS` was added, and CLAUDE.md gained two rules earned the hard way this cycle: never add an AI as a commit co-author, and scale verification to what a change could actually break rather than running full suites after editing a comment.
